The Chairman of IDPs in Chikun LGA, Comrade Adams Sule, told LEADERSHIP that the attacks occurred on Monday, November 16, in Agui Rido, Anguwan Suleja in Kaso Kakau Ward, and Kaso Kurmi community.
Sule said four persons were abducted from their residence in Agui Rido, including three children and an adult aged about 25.
He said the incident had left the family particularly vulnerable, as the father of two of the abducted children was reportedly bedridden due to illness.
In a separate attack at Anguwan Suleja, Kaso Kakau Ward, another resident was abducted.
According to Sule, the victim had previously been kidnapped by bandits and lost valuable property, including his motorcycle, to the attackers.
Sule said the attacks continued at about 8pm when armed men invaded Kaso Kurmi community, shooting and injuring one resident, who was subsequently hospitalised.
He added that four other persons were abducted during the attack, including two children aged one and three years.
Sule said the latest incidents had further heightened fear among residents who have endured repeated attacks, killings, abductions and destruction of property.
He said many households were facing economic hardship, indebtedness and the threat of hunger following repeated attacks and the disruption of their livelihoods.
He urged the authorities to develop a sustainable security and recovery plan to enable residents to return to their farms and rebuild their lives.
Meanwhile, a community official in Agui Rimi Kudensa, Danlami Yusuf, also confirmed the abduction of four persons in the community to LEADERSHIP.
Yusuf, who identified himself as the Secretary to the Village Head of Maraban Rido Kudensa, said the attack occurred at about 8:30pm on Monday.
Another resident of Kaso Kurmi, Ishaya Gana, also confirmed the abduction of four persons, including two women carrying children aged about four and six years.
The Kaduna State Police Command and the Ministry of Internal Security are yet to issue official statements on the attacks as of the time of filing this report.
